name: uptrack
description: Check and manage your Uptrack uptime monitoring from ChatGPT: view monitors, incidents, uptime and response times, check a site from several regions, and pause, resume, or acknowledge.

interface.longDescription:
Uptrack is an uptime monitoring service. This plugin connects ChatGPT to your Uptrack organization so you can check and manage your monitoring by chat.

What you can do:
- See all monitors with their current status, and open one monitor for detail and 30-day uptime.
- Read uptime percentages, daily uptime, and response-time percentiles (p50, p95, p99) for any monitor.
- Read recent check results for a monitor: time, status, HTTP code, response time, and the error for failed checks.
- Get dashboard totals: monitor counts, ongoing incidents, and 30-day uptime.
- List incidents (newest first, or only ongoing ones) and acknowledge an incident to pause its escalation reminders.
- List your status pages and your alert channels.
- Check whether any public website is up right now, from several regions, without creating a monitor.
- Create a monitor, change its name, URL, or interval, pause it, resume it, or delete it.
- Create an email, Slack, Discord, or Telegram alert channel.

How it works:
- You sign in with your Uptrack account and approve the permissions the plugin asks for. Read tools and write tools use separate permissions.
- Every tool works only inside the organization you signed in with.
- You need an Uptrack account. The plugin never asks for your Uptrack password.
- Tools that change or delete data are marked as such, so ChatGPT can ask you to confirm first.

Example requests: "Which of my monitors are down?", "Summarize my incidents from the last week", "Pause my staging monitor, then resume it", "Is example.com down right now?"
defaultPrompt: Which of my Uptrack monitors are down right now?
Summarize my Uptrack incidents from the last 7 days.
Is example.com down right now? Check it from several regions.

positive.description: Account overview: dashboard totals, monitors, status pages and alert channels.
positive.prompt: Give me an overview of my Uptrack account: how many monitors I have and their status, my status pages, and my alert channels.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls the read tools and answers with the 3 monitors and their current status, the overall 30-day uptime, the number of ongoing incidents, the status pages (if any), and the 1 email alert channel. No data is changed.

positive.description: Incident investigation: list incidents, then open the affected monitor and its recent checks.
positive.prompt: Show my recent Uptrack incidents. For the most recent one, tell me which monitor it affected and show that monitor's latest check results.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT lists the 1 incident with status, cause, start time and duration, identifies the affected monitor, and shows the monitor's most recent checks with time, status, HTTP code and response time. No data is changed.

positive.description: Performance analytics for one monitor over a chosen window.
positive.prompt: How did my first Uptrack monitor perform over the last 7 days? Give me uptime percent and response-time percentiles.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT finds the first monitor, then reports its uptime percent for 7 days, the daily uptime values, and the p50, p95 and p99 response times. No data is changed.

positive.description: Reversible write: pause a monitor, confirm it is paused, then resume it.
positive.prompt: Pause my first Uptrack monitor, confirm that it is paused, and then resume it right away.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT finds the monitor, pauses it, confirms the paused state, resumes it, and confirms it is active again. The monitor ends in the same state it started in.

positive.description: Acknowledge an incident (pauses escalation reminders only; it does not resolve the incident).
positive.prompt: Acknowledge my most recent Uptrack incident so escalation reminders stop.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT finds the most recent incident and acknowledges it. The reply confirms the incident id and that it is acknowledged. Repeating the call is safe.

negative.description: General knowledge question that has nothing to do with uptime monitoring.
negative.prompt: What is the weather in Hanoi this weekend?

negative.description: Infrastructure metrics and remediation request that Uptrack does not provide (no CPU metrics, no restarting servers).
negative.prompt: Show me the CPU usage of my Kubernetes pods and restart the ones that keep crashing.

negative.description: Coding task with no link to monitoring data.
negative.prompt: Write a Python function that reverses a linked list.

publication.release_notes: Initial release. Read your Uptrack monitors, incidents, status pages, alert channels, uptime analytics and recent checks from ChatGPT. Check any public website from several regions. Create, update, pause, resume and delete monitors, acknowledge incidents, and create alert channels. Sign in with OAuth; every tool works only in your own organization.
